chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs7001688
predictions: The variant will show no reproducible allele-dependent TF occupancy linked to a regulatory effect in relevant hepatic cells.
Any LDL association, if present, will be absent from these data or attributable to another linked variant or mechanism.
falsified_if: A relevant TF is shown to bind the variant with reproducible allele-dependent occupancy in hepatic cells, and variant editing produces a linked regulatory change.

chains.title: NME2 may gain binding at rs7001688 and affect CYP7A1 regulation
chains.element: The variant could lie in an unannotated regulatory sequence, but no cCRE overlaps it and NME2 occupancy at the site has not been measured.

links.claim: NME2 is a candidate because it is highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 and its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to alt T; however, occupancy is unknown, so this in-vitro result does not establish binding in cells.
A regulatory role for the sequence is unestablished: there is no overlapping cCRE or matching-biosample TF peak, and the reported CTCF peak is from LNCAP rather than HepG2.
CYP7A1 is a speculative target based on proximity; the supplied evidence does not connect this variant to CYP7A1 regulation.
NME2 is highly expressed in the stated cell line, but expression alone does not establish occupancy or a regulatory effect there.

A CYP7A1-mediated LDL effect is possible but unsupported for this variant; no variant-level GWAS association or significant GTEx eQTL is reported, and Open Targets reports no CYP7A1 association for the specified free-cholesterol measurement.

predictions: In relevant hepatic cells, NME2 occupancy at the site should be greater on T than G.
If CYP7A1 is the target, editing the variant should alter CYP7A1 expression; the direction of that expression change is not determined by the binding prediction.
falsified_if: A suitably sensitive assay finds no NME2 occupancy at the site in relevant hepatic cells.
Editing the variant produces no reproducible change in CYP7A1 expression or a linked regulatory readout.

chains.title: CASZ1 may gain binding at rs7001688 and affect FAM110B regulation
chains.element: The variant could fall in an unannotated regulatory sequence, but neither regulatory activity nor CASZ1 occupancy in hepatic cells is established.

links.claim: CASZ1's own QBiC-SELEX model predicts a strong alt-favoring binding change, but occupancy is unknown; CASZ1 was not assayed in matching HepG2 and its expression in the stated line is relatively low.
The evidence does not establish a regulatory element at the variant: no cCRE overlaps it and no matching-biosample TF peak is reported.
FAM110B is a speculative candidate because it is the closest listed gene; the pravastatin literature search hit does not establish FAM110B as a target of this variant.
CASZ1 is expressed at a relatively low level in Hep 3B2.1-7, and the supplied evidence does not show occupancy in this line or matching HepG2.
A FAM110B-mediated effect on LDL cholesterol is unsupported here; no variant-level GWAS association or significant GTEx eQTL is reported.

predictions: If this chain is correct, CASZ1 should occupy the site in relevant hepatic cells, with greater occupancy on T than G.
If FAM110B is the target, editing the variant should alter FAM110B expression; the direction is not inferable from the binding prediction.
falsified_if: CASZ1 shows no occupancy at the site in a suitably sensitive assay in relevant hepatic cells.
Editing the variant produces no reproducible change in FAM110B expression or a linked regulatory readout.

chains.title: CTCF occupancy may be slightly favored by the reference allele

links.claim: CTCF is expressed and has a reported peak over the variant in LNCAP, but its QBiC-SELEX model predicts only a small ref-favoring change below the detection gate at a weak site; this argues against a substantial allelic effect through CTCF binding.
The variant overlaps a CTCF ChIP-seq peak in LNCAP, but there is no matching HepG2 peak or overlapping cCRE, so regulatory function in hepatic cells is unestablished.
FAM110B is only a tentative target based on distance; neither the literature search hit nor the supplied evidence links it to this variant or to CTCF regulation.
CTCF is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, but the reported variant-overlapping occupancy is from LNCAP, not matching HepG2.
A CTCF-mediated effect on LDL cholesterol is unsupported; no variant-level GWAS association or significant GTEx eQTL is reported.

predictions: If this chain is correct, CTCF occupancy in relevant hepatic cells should be detectable and should be modestly greater on G than T.
If FAM110B is the target, perturbing the site should affect FAM110B expression, although the supplied evidence does not establish that target.
falsified_if: Relevant hepatic assays find no CTCF occupancy or no reproducible allele-dependent occupancy.

matrix.test: Measure allele-specific NME2 occupancy at rs7001688 by targeted CUT&RUN with amplicon sequencing in heterozygous Hep 3B2.1-7 cells.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent NME2 occupancy linked to the variant.
NME2 occupies the site and occupancy is greater on T than G.
No NME2-specific T-favoring occupancy; this chain instead predicts CASZ1 occupancy.
No NME2-specific T-favoring occupancy; this chain instead predicts CTCF occupancy, potentially modestly greater on G.

matrix.test: Test CASZ1 occupancy at rs7001688 by targeted CUT&RUN or ChIP-qPCR in HepG2 or Hep 3B2.1-7 cells.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible CASZ1 occupancy linked to the variant.
CASZ1 occupancy is detected; allele-specific follow-up should show greater occupancy on T.

matrix.test: Edit rs7001688 between G and T in Hep 3B2.1-7 cells and measure CYP7A1 and FAM110B expression.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible variant-dependent change in either gene is expected.
CYP7A1 expression changes reproducibly; the direction is not specified by the binding prediction.
FAM110B expression changes reproducibly; the direction is not specified by the binding prediction.
A FAM110B change is possible under the proposed target assignment, but the evidence gives little basis to expect one.

next_experiment: The highest-probability chain is H0 and the next is H1. The cheapest listed discriminating experiment is targeted allele-specific NME2 CUT&RUN with amplicon sequencing at rs7001688 in heterozygous Hep 3B2.1-7 cells. Greater NME2 occupancy on T would support H1 over H0, although occupancy alone would not establish a regulatory or LDL effect.
